explanation: EXISTS is appropriate when the outer query should keep a vendor if at least one related order meets the condition. Option A is correct because the subquery is correlated to the current vendor with o.vendor_id = v.vendor_id and checks for an order_total above 10000. Option B reverses the logic by returning vendors with no such orders. Option C compares vendor_id to order_total, which mismatches the columns. Option D is uncorrelated, so if any order over 10000 exists anywhere in the table, it would return every vendor.

options.text: WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders o WHERE o.vendor_id = v.vendor_id AND o.order_total > 10000)
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders o WHERE o.vendor_id = v.vendor_id AND o.order_total > 10000)
WHERE v.vendor_id IN (SELECT o.order_total FROM Orders o WHERE o.order_total > 10000)
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders o WHERE o.order_total > 10000)

prompt:
Assume the outer query is:
SELECT v.vendor_name
FROM Vendors v
...
A manager wants vendors who have at least one order over 10000, without joining Orders into the outer query. Which WHERE-clause condition correctly tests that requirement?
